21.text: Fall Slaughtering. — The cycle of “genuine sacrifices” is opened in the

22.text: fall with two “reindeer slaughterings” (qaanmaˊtɪrg̣ɪn). The first is called “thin

23.text: fawn-skin slaughtering” (wŭˊlha-qaanmaˊtɪrg̣ɪn); and the second, “making skins

24.text: for wearing [in the winter]” (têêtawñɪˊɪrg̣ɪn). As may be gathered from the

25.text: names, the practical purpose of both slaughterings is to obtain the annual

26.text: supply of skins for clothing. From the first slaughtering the thinner skins

27.text: are obtained. These serve for the finer dresses used by young people, and

28.text: they are also sold to the Russian traders. From the second slaughtering,

29.text: thicker skins are secured for use in all kinds of winter clothing.

30.text: The ceremonials which accompany both slaughterings are intended to

31.text: celebrate the re-union of the herd with the house after the summer separation,

32.text: and the beginning of their journeys together. They form the chief herd

33.text: ceremonial of the year. The essential features are, for the most part, the
